overview: The Kronenwetter Police and Fire Commission dismissed a complaint filed June 30, 2026, determining it did not rise to the level of termination, suspension, or demotion, voting 5-0. The commission also advanced two candidates, Andrew Phillips and Rebecca Kiey, in the firefighter/first responder hiring process following closed-session interviews, also by a 5-0 vote.

agenda.item: Closed session to interview Fire Department applicant(s) and consider personnel matters
Action after closed session: disposition of complaint and firefighter hiring process

discussions.body: Vice President Rick Smith moved, and Commissioner Donna Rule seconded, to approve the August 10, 2026 meeting minutes as written. The motion carried 5-0 by voice vote.

discussions.item: Closed Session — Fire Department Applicant Interviews and Personnel Matters
discussions.body: Vice President Smith moved, and Commissioner Lucene Udulutch seconded, to convene into closed session pursuant to Wis. Stat. 19.85(1)(f) and 19.85(1)(c) to interview Fire Department applicants and consider personnel matters. The motion carried 5-0 by roll call vote, and the commission entered closed session at 5:10 p.m., reconvening in open session at 6:42 p.m.

Following the closed session, Vice President Smith moved, and Commissioner Rule seconded, that the commission determined the complaint dated June 30, 2026 does not rise to the level of termination, suspension, or demotion, and therefore dismissed the complaint. The motion carried 5-0 by roll call vote.

Vice President Smith moved, and Commissioner Chet Rucinski seconded, to advance Andrew Phillips and Rebecca Kiey in the firefighter/first responder hiring process. The motion carried 5-0 by voice vote.

publicComment: Kenneth Charneski, of 2604 16th Road, Kronenwetter, appeared before the commission to voice concern over whether members of the commission were appropriately nominated and appointed by the Village Board.
